claim: The hood's crown carries 5 kN spread over its 500 mm cantilever below the 355 MPa yield of S355 with a factor of 1.5
law: Cantilever bending, sigma = M c / I; S355 yield 355 MPa (EN 10025-2, minimum for t up to 16 mm)

claim: The hood tip deflects less than 0.1 mm at 5 kN, so no contact with a head form
law: Cantilever with uniform load, d = w L^4 / (8 E I); E = 205 GPa

claim: The hood tip, taken as a flat strip across its 658 mm chord with no arch action, stays below yield with a factor of 1.5
law: Simply supported strip, sigma = (p c^2 / 8) / (t^2 / 6); conservative because the rolled crown carries part of the load as an arch
closed_by: SVD-CAL-001 B3 (membrane result); shell finite-element check or load test on CalRig at TRL 4

claim: Dragging the loaded train takes about 790 N at the rope (sledge friction plus rope on the floor)
law: Coulomb friction: F = mu_k m g for the sledges plus the drag of the rope on the floor and the sheave back tension

claim: A person turning the winch handle in high gear needs less than 200 N to start the loaded train
law: Winch power ratio and efficiency: handle force = rope force / (power ratio x efficiency); starting friction mu_s

claim: The 18 kN rope keeps a factor of 5 or more on the 2.5 kN release load after a 90 % splice (factor 5.04 at 70 %)
law: Rope breaking strength x splice efficiency / release load; factor 5 is working-line practice, not a cited standard (to confirm with the partner)

claim: The drill's slip clutch (35 N m) slips below the 2.5 kN swivel release in high gear
law: Rope force = clutch torque x power ratio x efficiency / drum radius; in low gear the same clutch would pass 4.8 kN, so the drill is used in high gear only

claim: Friction at the jacking pads holds the ring against twice the 2.5 kN release load with a factor of 1.5
law: Coulomb friction, F = mu N; the pad-to-pipe friction coefficient of 0.2 is an assumption for rusty or painted steel
closed_by: SVD-CAL-001 C8; friction coefficient to measure on CalRig at TRL 4; the friction coefficient 0.20 and the screw preload from a torque coefficient are assumptions (independent review)

claim: A 200 mm layflat duct passes 0.27 m3/s over 65 m with less than 600 Pa of loss, a pressure a 200 mm axial or mixed-flow portal blower can give
law: Darcy-Weisbach, dp = (f L / D + K) rho v^2 / 2, f = 0.030, K = 2.1 (SVD-CAL-001 F1)
closed_by: SVD-CAL-001 F1, F2; blower curve to confirm with the blower bought; no named blower curve yet: a 200 mm axial unit must pass 0.27 m3/s at about 570 Pa total (independent review)

claim: A right-angle drill on each portal winch moves loose spoil at least 0.4 m3/h, faster than a hand-dug face makes it
law: Cycle arithmetic: volume per trip / (out + unload + in + load + signals); drill speed from rpm and drum diameter

claim: Three people bring a 100 kg casualty out 60 m in under 5 minutes, hand over hand
law: Time = distance / speed (0.4 m/s hand over hand, ergonomics range) plus one minute to clip on
closed_by: SVD-CAL-001 E2; the 0.4 m/s hand-over-hand speed is an assumption; below 0.25 m/s the 5 min target fails; timed drill at TRL 4 (independent review)

claim: The kit goes up in less than 2 hours
law: Sum of the critical-path steps in SVD-CAL-001 G1; step times are estimates to measure in a drill at TRL 4

claim: The heaviest package weighs less than 40 kg
law: Sum of component masses from the model (cad/src/model.py masses())
closed_by: SVD-CAL-001 I2; the case itself is not counted

claim: 5 m3/min of fresh air per person is far more than needed to keep CO2 below 5,000 ppm
law: Dilution: Q = n x CO2 production / (limit - inlet); heavy work 1.5 L/min CO2 per person (physiology texts, to cite), inlet 400 ppm
closed_by: SVD-CAL-001 F2; heat and dust, not CO2, govern the airflow (SVD-CAL-001 F4)

claim: Four-gas monitors measure oxygen, carbon monoxide, hydrogen sulphide and flammable gas and alarm
law: Electrochemical cells for O2, CO and H2S and a catalytic bead or infrared cell for combustible gas are standard in portable four-gas monitors (Honeywell BW GasAlertMicroClip XL, listed at GBP 776.52 excluding VAT, checked 2026-11-02)
check: Commercial monitors exist; fitness for a collapse atmosphere (dust, humidity, calibration) to confirm with the rescue service

claim: Rope abrasion over 72 hours of hauling does not part the pull or tail rope
law: Polyester double braid dragged over a gritty steel floor: wear per kilometre is not predictable on paper; managed by a wear gauge each shift and a spare set (SVD-DDR-003 decision 25A)
check: About 250 round trips at the drill rate (SVD-CAL-001 H1); an endurance trial decides whether a tougher rope is needed

claim: UHMW-PE runners slide on the pipe floor with a friction coefficient of 0.30 sliding and 0.40 starting
law: UHMW-PE on dry steel is low friction (about 0.1 to 0.2 clean); grit, wet clay and rust raise it, so 0.30 and 0.40 are conservative assumptions
check: Not measurable on paper; sled test with pipe-floor debris at TRL 4

claim: The pull rope can carry a casualty with the 15:1 factor that life-safety rope practice uses (NFPA 1983, FireRescue1 summary)
law: Breaking strength x splice efficiency against 15 x the largest load the rope can see, which is the 2.5 kN swivel release, not the starting pull; NFPA 1983 (now in NFPA 2500) is a manufacturer standard and the 15:1 factor is a cited practice, not a requirement on this kit
check: Factor 6.5 on the 2.5 kN release (15 x 2.5 = 37.5 kN against 16.2 kN); 16.2 kN is 2.1 times the 7.8 kN that 15 x the starting pull of 519 N would need
closed_by: Proposed, awaiting Amish (SVD-DEC-001 open decision 4): a stretcher-only breakaway at 1.0 kN would give a factor of 16 on the rope; it changes the overload limit Amish decided, so it is not implemented

claim: Option B: a 40 x 40 x 4 mm aluminium T rail on sleepers 1 m apart carries a loaded wagon wheel below 6061-T6 yield with a factor of 3
law: Simply supported beam, M = P L / 4; sigma = M / Z; 6061-T6 yield 240 MPa (minimum, to confirm for the extrusion bought)
closed_by: SVD-OPT-001 Table 1; smallest section modulus and a dynamic factor of 2 at rail joints (independent review)

claim: Option B: rolling the train on rails (rolling resistance 0.02) cuts the pull to less than half of the sliding train
law: F = c_rr m g plus the same rope drag and back tension; c_rr = 0.02 for polymer wheels on aluminium rail (estimate, to confirm)

claim: Option B: cranked by hand, the rail train keeps ahead of the Silkyara face rate
law: Cycle arithmetic with the handle at its 60 rpm limit both ways (7.2 m/min); option A by hand makes 0.22 m3/h

claim: Option C, after the fix: a 7.5 kW three-phase high-pressure blower on a portal generator conveys lumps of up to 12 mm through 70 m of 150 mm hose
law: Conveying air at 1.5 times the terminal velocity v_t = sqrt(4 g d (rho_s - rho_a) / (3 C_d rho_a)), C_d = 1 (v_t = 18 m/s for 12 mm), solids loading doubles the air power; air power = Q dp, 60 % efficient. First draft: the 2.2 kW fan needed 2.5 kW for 6 mm fines and a lump of 50 mm needs 59 kW, so the first draft failed; the fix keeps suction extraction, limits the lump to 12 mm (the crew feeds the nozzle by hand) and sizes the blower on the pressure and flow the hose needs (SVD-DEC-001 D1)
closed_by: SVD-DEC-001 D1; a named blower curve passing about 1759 m3/h at 4.3 kPa is to assess
